dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: Claim 1 (probing/retrieval) has an honest fitting/eval story: the language logistic probe is scored with StratifiedKFold 5-fold CV (exp/02_analyze_bottleneck.py:59, cross_val_score), so fit/score splits are disjoint; retrieval is a parameter-free cosine ranking, no fitting. Claim 2 does contain a genuine leakage path: the English refusal direction is built from the FIRST 100 English MultiJail prompts (exp/04_refusal_direction.py:64 `df[source_lang].head(n_harm)`), while the English ASR evaluation uses df.head(40) of the SAME MultiJail file (exp/06_run_all_conditions.py:83 `pd.read_csv(...).head(40)`). Thus the 40 English eval prompts are a strict subset of the 100 prompts that defined the steering direction — in-sample evaluation for English. Mitigating factors: the direction is a single coarse mean-difference vector (not a per-prompt fit), and the load-bearing claim is cross-lingual TRANSFER to the other 9 languages, which are genuinely unseen by the English-only direction (the report's caveat block and interpretation §2 make this the central quantity). The benign anchor for the direction comes from m_mmlu/en (exp/04:24) whereas the MMLU capability eval uses a different file mmlu/all with a random 200-subset seed 0 (exp/09:66,86), so no MMLU overlap. The leakage is real but confined to 1 of 10 languages and does not touch the transfer conclusion.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: Two label systems, both valid and non-circular. Claim 1 ground truth is structural: language identity (used as probe target) and the parallel-translation correspondence (retrieval gold = same prompt id across languages, exp/02_analyze_bottleneck.py:43 gold=arange(N)); these are intrinsic to the MultiJail parallel corpus, not generated by the model under test, and directly operationalize 'geometry organized by meaning vs language'. Claim 2 ground truth is ASR from an LLM judge (gpt-5.4 via dmxapi, exp/08_llm_judge.py:19) that classifies each response REFUSED/HARMFUL/AMBIGUOUS with a strict rubric; ASR counts only HARMFUL (exp/10_analyze_claim2.py:36). The judge is an external model, NOT the LLaMA-3.1-8B under test, so labelling is non-circular, and this mirrors the paper's GPT-4o ASR pipeline (paper §5.1). Minor gaps: the AMBIGUOUS bucket (575/3200 responses) is dropped from ASR rather than partially counted (the report flags this in Caveats and points to claim2_agg_judge.csv), and gpt-5.4 substitutes for the paper's GPT-4o judge, introducing some evaluator noise. The metric nonetheless captures exactly what each claim asserts.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: The user-specified experiment-stage model is used exactly: /data/zhenqian/models/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is the hard default in every script (exp/01:23, exp/04:44, exp/06:52, exp/09:64), 32 layers / hidden 4096 confirmed in report.md:3, no downgrade to a smaller model despite the causal-proxy design. The specified primary dataset MultiJail is used from /data/zhenqian/data/multijail/MultiJail.csv (exp/06:53) with all 10 required languages [en,zh,it,vi,ar,ko,th,bn,sw,jv]. The task-specified judge model 'gpt-5.4' is honored (task.md:39, exp/08:19). MMLU is used for capability retention as the task permits. Deviations, all disclosed: MultiJail is subsetted to 200 prompts for Claim 1 and to 40 prompts/language for Claim 2 ASR (out of MultiJail's 315), and the paper's training resources (PKU-SafeRLHF, UltraFeedback, KTO training) are not consumed because the run substitutes a steering proxy for LASA training (report.md:14, discussed under Dim 9). No specified resource was silently swapped or shrunk in the main experiment; the subsetting is explicit and justified by the 10h GPU budget.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: Claim 1 rests on adequate scale: 200 parallel prompts x 10 languages = 2000 hidden vectors per layer across all 33 layers (results/claim1_layerwise.json, retrieval averaged over all 90 ordered language pairs). Claim 2 ASR rests on 40 prompts x 10 languages x 8 conditions = 3200 judged generations (verified: cache/main_sweep_judged.jsonl has 3200 rows, each gen file 400 lines). The aggregate mean-ASR direction is supported, but per-language ASR is thin: each cell is 40 items, so a figure like Swahili baseline 17.5% is 7/40 and the tier-level Delta claims (e.g. +0.075 low-resource) rest on ~40-160 items and single-digit HARMFUL counts (total HARMFUL across all 3200 = 99). MMLU uses 200 items. The report partially flags this ('40 prompts... Larger n would tighten the per-language numbers', Caveats), so the direction is credible but the per-language magnitudes are overstated relative to the sample. Borderline-thin per-cell evidence with only partial caveating.

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: Weakest dimension. All Claim 2 generation is greedy/deterministic (exp/06:110 do_sample=False), and every condition is a SINGLE run with a SINGLE steering direction; no multiple seeds, no bootstrap CIs, no significance test, and no error bars appear anywhere in report.md or the results/ products. The claimed differences are small and within plausible noise at n=40/language (tier deltas of +/-2.5 to 7.5 pp correspond to a 1-3 sample swing per cell). Claim 1's language probe does compute a 5-fold std (exp/02:61 returns scores.std()) but that std is neither stored in claim1_layerwise.json nor surfaced in the report. MMLU uses a single seed=0 subset (exp/09:68). The conclusions are therefore reported as point estimates whose robustness to randomness is unverified; the monotone alpha-trend across the sweep gives some informal robustness, but no formal uncertainty is quantified.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: Claim 2 is causal ('aligning safety at this layer YIELDS lower ASR') and the run backs it with a genuine intervention, not correlation: a forward hook adds alpha * unit-refusal-direction to the residual stream at a chosen decoder layer during generation (exp/06_run_all_conditions.py:33-40, ResidualSteer). It includes two real controls: (i) an injection-LOCATION control — bottleneck L14/L9 vs surface L28 — which is exactly the comparison the claim needs, and (ii) a coefficient sweep alpha in {3,5,8} showing a dose-response (mean ASR falls monotonically 2.75->1.50->1.25 at L14). The report honestly labels this a 'lightweight causal proxy' for LASA training (report.md:14). Missing rigor element: no random-direction / random-vector baseline to show the effect is specific to the refusal direction rather than to any residual perturbation of that norm (a norm-matched random steer could also suppress generation). This is the one absent control that keeps it from a 5.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: Every key number traces to a concrete on-disk product and agrees on recomputation. Claim 1: report's raw best retrieval 0.373 @ layer 9 matches results/claim1_layerwise.json retrieval_top1[9]=0.37283; raw lang-probe 0.999 matches lang_probe[9]; centered best 0.442 @ layer 16 matches results/claim1_centered.json retrieval_top1[16]=0.44178 with lang_probe[16]=0.0105 ('~0.010'); the last-layer spike to 0.62 matches centered retrieval_top1[32]=0.62356. Claim 2: I recomputed every condition mean-ASR from results/claim2_agg_judge.csv and got exactly the report's table (baseline 5.75, L14a3 2.75, L14a5 1.50, L14a8 1.25, L9a5 0.75, L9a8 0.25, surface 6.25/6.25). ASR aggregation is grounded in cache/main_sweep_judged.jsonl (3200 judged rows, 99 HARMFUL). MMLU numbers (0.635/0.590/0.325/0.640/0.640 and extra 0.645/0.320/0.290) match results/mmlu_capability.json + mmlu_capability_extra.json verbatim. Refusal direction is a real npz (cache/refusal_dir.npz, v/v_unit shape (33,4096)). No sourceless or back-filled numbers found.

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: The pipeline's records are self-consistent. The ASR table in report.md (lines 71-80) reproduces claim2_agg_judge.csv exactly (recomputed means identical to 4 decimals). The capability table (report.md:96-105) matches mmlu_capability.json and mmlu_capability_extra.json cell-for-cell (baseline 0.635, L14a3 0.645, L14a5 0.590, L14a8 0.325, L9a5 0.320, L9a8 0.290, surface 0.640). The 'mean ASR' column echoed in the MMLU table (0.0575, 0.0275, 0.0150, 0.0125, 0.0075, 0.0025, 0.0625, 0.0625) equals the independently recomputed per-condition means. Claim 1 report table matches both json products. Prose verdicts agree with the numbers (Claim 1 'confirmed', Claim 2 'supported' with the surface anti-transfer and L9 MMLU-collapse honestly stated). Only cosmetic slip: report.md:130 cites a stale reproduction path ('/data/zhenqian/Reproduction1/cc/...') that differs from the actual scientist1 tree — no numeric impact and no verdict conflict.

C1.claim: There exists an intermediate "semantic bottleneck" layer in multilingual LLMs whose hidden-state geometry is dominated by shared meaning rather than by language identity.

method.justification: 9a: The paper localizes the bottleneck via layer-wise Silhouette scores (semantic partition minus language partition) plus t-SNE (paper §3, Fig 3). The reproduction uses two complementary, directly interpretable probes instead: a language-identifiability logistic probe (5-fold CV) and cross-lingual parallel-translation retrieval top-1/MRR, on raw and per-language-mean-centered hidden states (exp/02_analyze_bottleneck.py). These are a valid, arguably more direct operationalization of 'geometry dominated by meaning vs language': high parallel-retrieval = semantic clustering, high lang-probe = language identity. The method family (representation-geometry probing) correctly matches the claim's mechanism category; the centered variant is a thoughtful control isolating additive language bias from semantic geometry. Departure from the paper's exact Silhouette metric does not weaken fit.

experiment.justification: 9b: Design is complete for this claim: all 33 layers (embedding + 32 blocks) analyzed, 200 parallel prompts x 10 languages, retrieval averaged over all 90 ordered language pairs, explicit chance baselines stated (lang chance 10%, retrieval chance ~0.5%), and raw-vs-centered contrast to separate additive language shift from semantic content (results/claim1_layerwise.json, results/claim1_centered.json). The probe uses proper cross-validation (StratifiedKFold). The per-pair heatmap checks that no single high-resource pair drives the average. Metric strictly corresponds to the claim. Only minor omission: no Silhouette/t-SNE cross-check against the paper's own statistic and no reported variance on the retrieval curves, but the evidence base is strong and criteria were fixed a priori.

result.justification: 9c: Qualitatively agrees with the paper. Paper places the LLaMA-3.1-8B semantic bottleneck at layer 14 (43.8% depth, Table 4). The reproduction finds semantic (centered) retrieval peaking at layers 14-16 and sustained high from ~layer 8-24, with language identifiability collapsing from 0.999 to ~0.010 after mean-subtraction, and concludes a bottleneck region of layers 9-16 (28-50% depth) — which contains the paper's layer 14. The nuance that raw hidden states still fully encode language (lang-probe 0.999) while semantics dominate only after removing the additive language mean is disclosed honestly and actually enriches the paper's picture rather than contradicting it. Verdict 'confirmed' is well grounded.

C2.claim: Aligning safety at this layer yields substantially lower attack success rates across high-, medium-, and low-resource languages (including languages unseen during alignment training) compared with surface-level safety alignment baselines, while preserving general task performance.

method.justification: 9a: The paper's mechanism is LASA — a Safety Semantic Interpreter trained on the bottleneck plus KTO-style semantic-conditioned generation (paper §4). The reproduction substitutes a lightweight causal proxy: an English-only refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024, harmful-minus-benign mean of last-token hidden states, exp/04_refusal_direction.py) injected via a residual-stream hook at bottleneck (L14/L9) vs surface (L28) layers (exp/06). This is a legitimate and well-motivated method for testing the CORE directional claim — whether the bottleneck layer carries a language-agnostic safety signal that transfers from one high-resource language to unseen languages — and it is honestly disclosed as a proxy. It is nonetheless a substantial departure: steering is not 'alignment/training', it exercises a single fixed direction rather than a learned interpreter, and the 'aligning' verb in the claim is only proxied. Suitable-but-weaker than the paper's method.

experiment.justification: 9b: Reasonable, moderately complete design. Conditions cover baseline, bottleneck L14 alpha{3,5,8}, bottleneck L9 alpha{5,8}, and surface L28 alpha{3,5} (exp/06 / results/claim2_agg_judge.csv), giving both the load-bearing location control (bottleneck vs surface) and a dose-response sweep. Cross-lingual transfer is tested exactly as the claim requires: the direction is English-only and evaluated on 9 unseen languages, binned into high/med/low tiers (exp/10). Capability retention is measured with MMLU under the same steering (exp/09), addressing 'preserving general task performance'. The judge criterion (HARMFUL=ASR) is fixed a priori, not retuned. Shortfalls that cap this: n=40/language is thin and single-seed (Dim 4/5), only one surface layer is probed, and there is no norm-matched random-direction control to isolate direction-specific effects; alpha exploration is adequate but modest.

result.justification: 9c: The result qualitatively reproduces the paper's central findings. (1) Bottleneck steering transfers cross-lingually: L14 lowers mean ASR from 5.75% to 1.25-2.75% with the largest reductions on the low-resource tier (Delta up to +0.075), matching the paper's headline that LASA improves safety across all languages with the strongest gains on unseen low-resource languages. (2) Surface steering fails/anti-transfers: L28 leaves mean ASR ~6.25% and pushes Swahili UP from 17.5% to 27.5-30% (low-resource Delta negative), directly echoing the paper's argument that last-layer interventions are language-dominated and do not generalize. (3) Capability is preserved at moderate strength (L14 alpha=3 MMLU 0.645 vs 0.635 baseline), with the honest caveat that deep/strong steering (L9) collapses MMLU to 0.29 — a transparent trade-off, not disguised. Absolute ASR magnitudes differ from the paper (baseline 5.75% here vs vanilla ~21-24.7% in the paper, due to the strict judge, greedy decoding and n=40 subset), and the per-language effects are noisy, but the DIRECTION and the qualitative story match the paper faithfully and are honestly analyzed; no goalpost-tuning or disguised disagreement is evident.
